paper_metadata.title: Gravitational wave matched filtering by quantum Monte Carlo integration and quantum amplitude amplification

summary: This paper proposes a gate-based quantum algorithm for gravitational-wave matched filtering that replaces FFT-based SNR evaluation with quantum Monte Carlo integration and uses quantum amplitude amplification to search over Ntemp templates and M coalescence times. The main asymptotic result is a qubit count scaling polylogarithmically in M and a query complexity of order gamma*M/((rho_hard-rho_soft)*sqrt(r(rho_hard)))) up to logarithmic factors, with the illustrative thresholds rho_soft = 8 and rho_hard = 9.

experiments.description: Quantum algorithm for gravitational-wave matched filtering using quantum Monte Carlo integration for SNR estimation and quantum amplitude amplification to search over templates and coalescence times.

algorithm.variant: QMCI-based matched filtering with QAA search

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Template index m and coalescence-time index j are placed in uniform superposition; frequency-bin values are loaded via qRAM/arithmetic oracles to estimate the SNR mean over k.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Find any (m,j) such that rho_{m,j} >= rho_hard with high probability; output a pair with rho_{m,j} >= rho_soft.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Two-threshold acceptance rule: templates with true SNR >= rho_hard should be accepted; templates with true SNR < rho_soft should be rejected; intermediate region may be either.

problem_instance.description: Gravitational-wave matched filtering over a template bank and discrete coalescence times.

dataset_specification.description: Detector output s(t)=h(t)+n(t); frequency-domain data \u007e s(f_k) and noise PSD S_n(f)

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discrete Fourier transform of detector output; normalization by PSD; template normalization (Q|Q)=1; QRAM loading of frequency-domain data.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical analysis only; no numerical benchmark or hardware experiment reported.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical FFT-based matched filtering used as baseline/comparison; QRAM assumed for data loading.
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical preparation of detector-output frequency data in QRAM; template-bank construction from waveform models.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure first two registers after QAA, then classically compute rho_{m,j} to verify rho_{m,j} >= rho_soft.

speedup_claims.conditions: with respect to template number; assuming fault-tolerant quantum computing and the stated oracles/qRAM access
speedup_claims.caveats: The speedup is asymptotic and depends on the fraction of matching templates r(rho_hard) or r(rho_th); logarithmic factors are hidden in eO notation.

speedup_claims.conditions: replacing FFT with QMCI for SNR estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a qubit-count scaling claim, not a runtime speedup; it relies on qRAM and arithmetic oracles.

speedup_claims.conditions: for r(rho_hard) > 0, up to logarithmic factors
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper also states the same order as the previous FFT-based quantum algorithm in terms of M, while reducing qubit requirements.

speedup_claims.conditions: for r(rho_hard) = 0 or in the worst-case no-signal regime, up to logarithmic factors
speedup_claims.caveats: This is the query complexity stated for the quantum algorithm in the no-signal case; it is compared against O(Ntemp * M log M) classically.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(M log M / r(rho_th)) for r(rho_th)>0 and O(Ntemp*M*log M) when r(rho_th)=0

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not reported; no empirical crossover analysis is provided.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Asymptotic gate-based quantum algorithm with qRAM and arithmetic oracles; qubit count scales polylogarithmically in M, but runtime still depends on gamma, (rho_hard-rho_soft), and 1/sqrt(r).
limiting_factors: Quadratic speedup only, which Hoefler-style constant-factor analysis typically deems non-viable on near-term hardware
Complexity depends on hidden logarithmic factors and on gamma/(rho_hard-rho_soft)

notes: The paper is theoretical and does not report an actual hardware run, circuit depth, gate counts, shots, or transpilation details.
The qubit count is given asymptotically in Eq. (39); no concrete numeric qubit count is reported.

The paper claims a theoretical quadratic speedup in template search and an exponential reduction in qubit count versus FFT-based matched filtering, but provides no empirical benchmark or hardware demonstration.
